extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, and health researchers
extracted.subtask_short: using reporting guidelines in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and applying reporting guidelines and checklists when reviewing or preparing health-research manuscripts to improve transparency and completeness of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a reporting guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: A reporting guideline is 'A checklist, flow diagram, or structured text to guide authors in reporting a specific type of research, developed using explicit methodology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting guidelines may take the form of checklists, flow diagrams, or structured text; they are developed using explicit methodology. The EQUATOR Network hosts over 400 reporting guidelines and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: improve value and reliability of published health research
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Network aims to improve the value and reliability of published health research by promoting transparent and accurate reporting and wider use of high-quality, robust reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reporting guidelines to increase transparency and accuracy of manuscripts, thereby improving research value and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer toolkit content
rubrics_metrics.description: The toolkit includes template instructions to peer reviewers and editable versions of common checklists with additional explanation for reviewers to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers should use the provided templates and editable checklists (with reviewer-focused explanations) to assess completeness of reporting; journals and reviewers can adapt these templates to local workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal practice: first-reviewer compliance check
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals that have implemented reporting guidelines ask a first peer reviewer to check guideline compliance before recruiting additional reviewers, and if the manuscript fails, peer review halts and the article is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may triage submissions by an initial compliance check against the relevant guideline; failure to meet core reporting items can justify returning the manuscript without full peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the appropriate guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'Identify the appropriate guideline for the study type.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which reporting guideline (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE) applies based on the study design and manuscript type before performing a checklist-based review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the manuscript against the guideline's checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'Check the manuscript against the guideline's checklist.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically compare manuscript sections to each checklist item to verify whether required information is present and sufficiently detailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note missing, unclear, or inadequately reported items
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'Note items that are missing, unclear, or inadequately reported.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checklist items are absent or ambiguously reported, record specific examples and explain what additional information or clarification is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend completing the checklist for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'Recommend the authors complete the checklist for resubmission.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors to provide a completed checklist (often with page/line references) to demonstrate how each reporting item has been addressed on revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT — Randomized trials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT when evaluating or reporting randomized controlled trials to ensure key trial-design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation elements are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA — Systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply PRISMA for systematic reviews and meta-analyses to check for transparent reporting of search methods, eligibility criteria, study selection, synthesis, and bias assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE — Observational studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STROBE for cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional observational studies to ensure reporting of study design, participants, variables, bias, study size, statistical methods, and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE — Animal research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ARRIVE guidelines when reviewing animal research to ensure reporting of experimental procedures, animal characteristics, housing, and welfare, and measures to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRQR / COREQ — Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SRQR or COREQ for qualitative studies to verify reporting of research team, study design, data collection, analysis, and methodological rigor specific to qualitative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE — Case reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply CARE guidelines for case reports to ensure clear reporting of patient information, clinical findings, diagnostic assessments, interventions, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT — Trial protocols
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT when assessing trial protocols to verify comprehensive reporting of trial objectives, design, methodology, statistical considerations, and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD — Diagnostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply STARD for diagnostic accuracy studies to ensure transparent reporting of index tests, reference standards, participant selection, and measures of diagnostic performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD — Prediction models
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TRIPOD for studies developing or validating prediction models to check reporting of model development, performance, validation, and clinical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS — Health economic evaluations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply CHEERS for economic evaluations to ensure reporting of perspective, comparators, time horizon, costs, outcomes, and analytic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE — Practice guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGREE to appraise reporting and development of clinical practice guidelines, including scope, stakeholder involvement, rigor, clarity, applicability, and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ENTREQ — Qualitative research synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: ENTREQ — Enhancing transparency in qualitative research synthesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ENTREQ for synthesizing qualitative research to ensure transparent reporting of search, appraisal, synthesis methods, and interpretation of qualitative findings.
